note: HHs the coordinator proposes for Vivian to vet. The dashboard's 'HHs to vet' panel shows them; a click records the decision here and in vetting_decisions.jsonl. Approved items go to the H queue (promotion-shortlist.md) when the coordinator promotes them.

items.title: Culture beyond composition: the emergent slow mode
items.why: The cleanest test of whether the village is more than the sum of its members' own vectors. Uses DQ5 vectors only.

items.title: Remanence: the endogenous part of the mean field
items.why: Day-1 content leaning toward the previous period, beyond kickoff and agent priors. Newcomers tell record vs memory.

items.title: Enculturation of newcomers
items.why: Do newcomers drift toward a village-specific culture, faster with more veteran reads? Uses every roster join.

items.title: History-search outage as a collective-memory scramble
items.why: A dated natural Kolchinsky intervention (03-31/04-01). One event, cheap, a clean positive or a clean zero.

items.title: Repos recruit hosts by their own state
items.why: Tests if repo state recruits agents beyond goal naming and share. H77/H78 show share and naming dominate; this asks what remains.

items.title: Autonomy across scales with the impostors as environment
items.why: The one formal information test: where does self-prediction peak, agent to village, against size-matched nulls.

items.title: Scaling of outputs with N (replies ∝ N^1.34 from H18)
items.why: A consistency check of H18's dilution law and a direct test of collective benefit (work ∝ N^>1?).

items.title: Taylor's law as a shared-field gauge
items.why: One number per unit for the shared-field share. Becomes a standard column for every hypothesis.

items.title: κ table: commits per bit by channel
items.why: The flagship Kolchinsky number: what each information channel is worth. H70 builds the artifact row now.

items.title: Collective memory decays biexponentially
items.why: Fast decay carried by veterans, slow decay carried by the record. The slow part is the village's cultural memory.

items.title: Price equation: selection, transmission, migration
items.why: Splits culture change into influence, bias and roster turnover. Separates culture from migration.

items.title: Collective entropy production beyond the parts
items.why: A collective arrow of time that individuals lack. Uses the Aguilera estimator; pairs with H76.

items.title: Eigenvector rotation as a reorganization signal
items.why: A spectral alarm for goal and platform changes. A direct rival for H74's detector.

items.title: RMT-cleaned matrices forecast tomorrow's alignment
items.why: Out-of-sample test that the talk and content modes (H12) carry real structure beyond noise.

items.title: Project choice as a Brock–Durlauf equilibrium
items.why: Fits utility and social coupling for project choice; predicts multiple equilibria across same-type weeks.

items.title: Work allocation as a max-entropy equilibrium
items.why: A principled null for H06/H11 allocations. Deviations measure planning or herding in bits.

items.title: Speed-limit slack as a kickoff-specificity gauge
items.why: H75 found named-target kickoffs settle at the speed limit (S ≈ 1). Test S as a one-number gauge of how much a goal constrains allocation.

items.title: Goal switches show hysteresis: a coercive field
items.why: After a goal change, alignment with the old goal lags by an amount that grows with how ordered the old state was. Gives a coercive field and an inertia time; tells operators whether to clear context at a switch.

items.title: A restoring-force law for the kickoff quench
items.why: Each agent's day-1 displacement ∝ its distance from the kickoff target: Δv = χ_i(k̂ − v). An unfitted shape test, and a per-agent susceptibility χ_i to set beside style's agent constant.

items.title: Conflicting kickoff cues quench into two domains
items.why: Two-target kickoffs or different room instructions (#38, #44) give bimodal day-1 positions with a domain wall at the room boundary.

items.title: #51 is a random-field system
items.why: The natural successor to the refuted spin glass (H22): private roles are random fields, the room is a weak mean-field pull. Predicts the overlap distribution, and rivals co-moving through shared niches.

items.title: Fluctuations predict relaxation (mean-field Glauber)
items.why: βJ₀ from fluctuations should predict how fast responses decay: τ = τ₀/(1 − βJ₀(1−m²)). A fluctuation–relaxation consistency test on the talk and content channels, where coupling is real.

items.title: Goals act on a two-state order parameter
items.why: Rescues H10 in Ising form: on the on-goal occupancy p(t), a Legendre tilt does predict variance growth while p < ½. Linear response may hold on the right variable.

items.title: Prompt-held targets persist, chat-held targets decay
items.why: Remanence time scales with how often the target re-enters context: the system prompt or memory (#51 private goals, persistent) vs chat (kickoffs, decaying). A field-refresh law.

items.title: #best/#rest: explicit vs spontaneous symmetry breaking
items.why: Separates the response to the operator's room field from spontaneous divergence that persists after members swap rooms (NE19 moves).

items.title: Pairwise Ising vs full multi-information in co-usage
items.why: Schneidman's test: does a pairwise max-ent model capture the swarm's co-usage (I₂/I_N > 0.9)? A higher-order remainder beyond fields would be collective structure.

items.title: Phenomenological RG of the dialect (Bialek–Meshulam)
items.why: Coarse-grain thousands of term time series. β̃ (free energy of silence) and τ_c scaling separate a field from a non-trivial fixed point.

items.title: Barkhausen avalanches when a field is stepped
items.why: Do project switches after kickoffs and human messages come in power-law bursts (random-field Ising crackling, τ ≈ 1.5), with Poisson switching between steps?

items.title: Nights demagnetize: remanence decays per night
items.why: Overnight consolidation acts as AC demagnetization: remanence falls in steps at nights, and the night-count clock beats active hours. Pairs with H82.

items.title: Domain walls between rooms, set by bridging agents
items.why: Rooms with different instructions form two content domains. Agents who hop rooms sit in the wall, and its width grows with their reads. H41 1b: #51 hoppers leak about half the time.

items.title: Two outside channels that could fake H81's slow mode: public chat (NE39) and providers
items.why: NE39 cut ~100 public messages a day to ≤ 4; if H81's slow mode is an outside drift it should weaken after the cut, and a provider drift would ride on same-lab pairs only.

items.title: Does culture age while the village sleeps? A clock test for H81
items.why: Endogenous culture can only decorrelate while agents run, an outside drift decorrelates on calendar days; refit H81's decay on active vs calendar time.

items.title: The slow mode's decay time should grow with N (finite-magnet wandering)
items.why: A finite magnet's direction diffuses at a rate ∝ 1/N, while an outside drift does not care about N; size-matched subsets remove the estimation-noise fake.

items.title: Room split: grows from zero (instability) or appears at once (hidden field)?
items.why: True symmetry breaking starts at zero separation and picks its direction from early noise; a hidden work field gives full separation on day 1 along a direction the old repos predict. This turns H100's residual into a test.

items.title: Goldstone wandering: spontaneous room directions drift, fielded ones stay pinned
items.why: With no field the ordered direction costs nothing to rotate, so it diffuses; compare day-to-day rotation in identical-kickoff vs room-specific-kickoff weeks.

items.title: Forced erasure as a demagnetizing pulse: where is the room's order stored?
items.why: If room order is coupling held in context, alignment with the room drops right after a forced wipe (NE41, quasi-random timing) and recovers with re-reads; if it is a self-made repo field, it does not drop.

items.title: Exchange bias: the own artifact shifts an agent's goal-switch loop
items.why: A pinned layer shifts a hysteresis loop; agents still committing to their own repo at a goal boundary should carry the old goal ≥ 2× longer, with NE24 (repo host swap) as the confirmatory cut.

items.title: Sum rule for talk: Fano factor = 1/(1 − g)²
items.why: A parameter-free check that H67's read-out gain explains all talk clustering after trimming; any excess Fano is a field or a coupling the read-out loop misses.

items.title: Crossing claims anti-coordinate: parallel updates make 2-cycles
items.why: Agents who pile onto a project with messages crossing in flight should both leave again (a Little-model 2-cycle), while sequential pile-ons stick; a read vs in-flight partition contrast.

items.title: Data collapse of kickoff settling on each agent's own call clock
items.why: If agents update only at calls, per-agent settling is one exponential in own calls, and the swarm's 4.5-h settling curve follows from the call-rate mix with no new parameter.

items.title: Read-out channel capacity: information per call grows as k^0.34
items.why: H18's dilution predicts batch uptake ∝ k^(1−β) and H59 says one read is one kick; one Gaussian-MI curve over the ledger tells which law holds.

items.title: A Griffiths phase: rare strong pairs give a subcritical swarm heavy-tailed talk
items.why: Subcritical on average but locally supercritical ping-pong dyads would give non-geometric reply-chain tails that vanish when those pairs are removed.
